Occupied by task 0: base subjects care_premium_charge, care_claim_recovery and care_claim_payout;
policies care_ext_outstanding_loading_charge, care_ext_supplier_recovery_declaration and
care_ext_settled_benefit_payment; tools charge_destination_loading_6e26c317,

Claimed by this task, all previously unoccupied: base subjects care_insured_amend,
care_premium_adjustment and care_claim_file; policies care_ext_declared_cost_restatement,
care_ext_reration_difference and care_ext_cancellation_claim_intake; tools
restate_declared_trip_cost_4b2fbffa, raise_rating_adjustment_56692b3c and

This is the final task of the difficulty, so no headroom needs to be reserved. Union check: the two
tasks' scopes are pairwise disjoint and together cover all six extended policies and all six task

DESIGN THESIS
Surface goal the customer volunteers: "we had to give the holiday up and I want to claim on the
travel insurance." That points at one problem only — filing the cancellation claim, which is the
traveller's own act in her own name.
The genuinely scored core parameter: claimed_amount_usd on that filing.
Between the goal and that number the policy puts two prerequisites the customer never mentions:
 (1) the amount claimed is measured on the declared trip cost the certificate carries, and the
     certificate still declares the tour's original quoted price although the underwriting desk
     approved a correction in June and the package's ledger has moved a long way since;
 (2) a claim is filed for an amount only after the certificate's premium lines carry the re-rating
     its corrected particulars call for, and no adjustment line stands on the certificate at all.
Depth: goal -> claim amount -> the declared cost -> the package ledger; and goal -> claim amount ->
the re-rating -> the declared cost -> the package ledger. Breadth: the claim reads the package's
status, its credit, its deposit terms and the day it was given up; the restatement reads the
package's whole routine ledger, its refund form, its credit horizon and its party; the re-rating
reads the certificate's own premium lines, the approved request's evidence and the package's last
routine line.
Observable terminal state: the certificate declares a corrected trip cost, its premium lines carry a
re-rating adjustment, and one claim stands filed against the cancellation benefit.

CHECK CARD 1 — BASE-INVARIANT CARD
subject care_insured_amend:
  care_policy_amendment — one structured gate, upgrade_approved (kind authorization): "Cover is
    upgraded only when the underwriting desk has already recorded an approved cover upgrade against
    this policy", evidenced by care_policy_requests.request_status and correlated to the action's
    care_request_id. It is satisfied at frozen_time by care_policy_requests.d61c4a10-e061-499c-a404-ad96f7ae4641, an approved
    decision of the underwriting desk standing against this certificate, and the gold call passes
    that request's reference as care_request_id. Three clauses of that policy are replaced in
    overwrite, and the timing clauses are two of them. The certificate's own record does NOT say the
    journey was never taken: care_policies.e2326376-824b-443f-8e1b-46046f2a9a05.status is expired
    and its trip dates of 2026-08-20 to 2026-09-03 are both past at frozen_time, and under the base
    lifecycle expired is reachable only through in_force, so the record asserts that the journey
    began and ended. Base's "No amendment is accepted once the journey has begun or once a claim has
    been filed, because the risk is then no longer uncertain." would therefore bar this write, and
    base's "A declared particular of the risk may be corrected while the policy stands, and the
    premium follows the correction from the day it takes effect." would leave it arguable. Both are
    named in overwrite and replaced by sentences of this policy's own rule: a correction the
    underwriting desk has approved is carried onto the certificate whenever it is found, whether or
    not the journey insured has begun or ended, because it restates what the journey actually
    carried rather than altering the risk; and the correction is made on a certificate standing in
    any state other than cancelled, the expired state included. This certificate is not cancelled —
    cancelled_at is empty, and it is the PACKAGE that stands cancelled — so the replacement clause
    admits the write and no sentence a reader reaches bars it. Every other clause of
    care_policy_amendment stands and is checked against this world: no claim has been filed on the
    certificate at the moment the correction is made, which is why the correction must be made
    BEFORE the claim is filed and can never be made after.
subject care_premium_adjustment:
  care_premium_rating — no structured eligibility gate. One clause replaced in overwrite (the pro
    rata sentence); the rest stand, in particular the minimum-premium clause (the certificate's
    premium already stands far above TripGuard Premier's 109.00 minimum) and "The policy fee is
    charged once per certificate however many travellers are named, and is never returned", which is
    why the policy fee is left out of the premium the difference is measured against.
subject care_claim_file:
  care_claim_filing — three structured gates, all inherited unchanged (this policy's overwrite is
    []): incident_date_stated (caller_fact) is satisfied by the traveller stating the day she gave
    the trip up; policy_covers_the_incident (state, allowed in_force or expired) is satisfied because
    care_policies.e2326376-824b-443f-8e1b-46046f2a9a05.status is expired; one_claim_per_reference (dedup) is satisfied because the
    certificate carries no claim at all, so no row carries reference TC-9048-26. Its other clauses
    stand: the claim is filed within the plan's 45-day filing deadline counted from the incident
    (2026-08-14 plus 45 days is 2026-09-28, and frozen_time is 2026-09-17), and one incident touching
    one benefit is filed as one claim.
TIME GATES: the care charter carries exactly one time eligibility, care_free_look.inside_free_look,
which applies_to care_cancel. None of this task's three subjects is care_cancel, so there is no time
gate to inherit and temporal_feasibility is []. The 45-day filing deadline lives in
care_claim_filing's prose rather than in a structured time eligibility, and it is checked by hand
above and in seed_consistency.

CHECK CARD 2 — BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
The narrowest object the request points at is the insured journey on certificate WLC5602841 —
initial_state.care_policies.e2326376-824b-443f-8e1b-46046f2a9a05 — and the vacation package it was bought alongside,
initial_state.bundle_packages.dbff8373-1232-4db1-a57c-d0b30a507e6a, which the certificate names through linked_bundle_package_id
and which names the certificate back through linked_care_policy_id. That two-way link is the
correlation key: it is why the package's ledger, and no other package, fixes the outlay.
Rows that enter the aggregates, and why they belong:
  - the prepaid outlay: the six package lines whose reason is the package's routine terms (9490078c-d2b1-4418-8c4b-67862921de58,
    2163c0b0-e3c3-4985-b548-2fc6caa608bb, 78eaf32c-4d31-4bdb-9de3-364c18808a33, 8c88ca7c-16d9-4f95-a354-eef7ab31601e, 5d18657a-2081-4f17-a38f-d2cdf39a2080, e380da3b-ed49-43f4-8229-7c49a03e7ec5), less the agency service fee 2163c0b0-e3c3-4985-b548-2fc6caa608bb.
  - the amounts the operator has returned otherwise than on the surrender of the journey, which is
    what the restatement takes off the outlay: the price-guarantee payout
    041a3310-6974-4ba7-a886-d93fcc7fd7d3 alone. The cancellation credit
    d7a1c870-e2a1-4187-8b09-c40ae60d68bf is left out there because it was given back on the surrender
    itself, and the rule says so outright.
  - the value the operator has given back, which is what the CLAIM takes off: that same payout
    041a3310-6974-4ba7-a886-d93fcc7fd7d3 together with the cancellation credit
    d7a1c870-e2a1-4187-8b09-c40ae60d68bf, because the claim answers the loss rather than the
    declaration.
  - the premium already charged: the certificate's four premium lines 587508bb-cdef-4dae-9a10-193f7ca3bb27, 7b5223ce-7572-4be8-a4e6-24c95e50a3fb, 46ce914f-376b-469b-90ca-908df87a84a0 and
    08c6e641-3280-4eb6-b31e-2139b96c54f8, less the policy fee 08c6e641-3280-4eb6-b31e-2139b96c54f8.
Rows that are excluded and how: the cancellation credit d7a1c870-e2a1-4187-8b09-c40ae60d68bf and the price-guarantee payout 041a3310-6974-4ba7-a886-d93fcc7fd7d3
carry reasons other than the package's routine terms, so neither enters the prepaid outlay — they are
value returned, not value laid out, and the rule separates the two by the reason the line carries.
The declined upgrade request 1bd3795f-52e3-4407-aad1-af66367f88a3 is excluded because the ceiling rule reads only a correction the
desk has approved, and that request was declined; it is the near-miss a careless reader takes for the
authority to amend.
The tool writes the correlation back: the restatement passes the approved request's reference, and
the adjustment passes the base premium line it re-rates as source_entry_id.

  topological order: care_ext_declared_cost_restatement, care_ext_reration_difference,

  per-edge deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run, figures below): skipping the restatement moves the

STEP 1 — POLICIES (see care.extended.yaml)
FACTOR CARD — care_ext_declared_cost_restatement (4 factors; scored corrected_trip_cost_usd = 18436.50)
 * outlay_evidence_basis (method, cross_difficulty bundle). Ladder: a balance-settling line and a
   package standing confirmed, travelling, completed or cancelled -> the routine ledger less the
   agency fee; no balance-settling line and such a standing -> the amount the package records as
   paid; otherwise -> the package's quoted price. Tier taken: the first. Evidence rows:
   bundle_ledger_entries.5d18657a-2081-4f17-a38f-d2cdf39a2080 (the final payment) and bundle_packages.dbff8373-1232-4db1-a57c-d0b30a507e6a.status = cancelled,
   with the routine lines summing to 25791.80 and the agency fee 2163c0b0-e3c3-4985-b548-2fc6caa608bb at 99.80, giving 25692.00.
   Baseline reading: the quoted price of 17900.00; result then 12592.50.
 * returned_value_recognition (parameter, cross_difficulty bundle). Ladder: value returned to the
   original form of payment with an amount returned -> in full; value returned only as a future
   travel credit whose credit may still be redeemed after the last day of the journey -> three
   quarters; otherwise -> nothing. Tier taken: the second. Evidence rows:
   bundle_packages.dbff8373-1232-4db1-a57c-d0b30a507e6a.refund_form = future_travel_credit and
   bundle_ledger_entries.d7a1c870-e2a1-4187-8b09-c40ae60d68bf.credit_expires_on = 2028-02-14 against the certificate's
   trip_end_date of 2026-09-03, so the price-guarantee payout of -1480.00 (041a3310-6974-4ba7-a886-d93fcc7fd7d3) is recognised at
   -1110.00. Baseline reading: nothing recognised; result then 19250.00 (the ceiling then bites).
 * insured_party_share (parameter, cross_difficulty bundle). Ladder: the certificate names fewer
   travellers than the package's party and the package carries no child -> the share the named
   travellers bear of the party; fewer named and at least one child -> the share they bear of the
   adults; otherwise -> the whole of it. Tier taken: the first. Evidence:
   care_policies.e2326376-824b-443f-8e1b-46046f2a9a05.insured_count = 3 against bundle_packages.dbff8373-1232-4db1-a57c-d0b30a507e6a.party_adults = 4 and
   party_children = 0, giving 75 per cent. Baseline reading: the whole of it; result then 19250.00.
 * declared_ceiling_basis (parameter). Ladder: an approved correction stating a cost at or above the
   outlay taken -> the plan's ceiling; an approved correction stating a cost below it -> the figure
   the correction states; otherwise -> the package's quoted price. Tier taken: the first. Evidence
   row: care_policy_requests.d61c4a10-e061-499c-a404-ad96f7ae4641.requested_trip_cost_usd = 19250.00, which is at or above the
   18436.50 taken, so TripGuard Premier's ceiling of 35000.00 applies and does not bite. Baseline
   reading: the quoted price of 17900.00; result then 17900.00.
 Whole-baseline fall-back: 17900.00 — exactly the figure the certificate already carries, which is
   why an agent who reads only the computation document concludes nothing needs correcting at all.
 Near-miss planted: care_policy_requests.1bd3795f-52e3-4407-aad1-af66367f88a3 is a DECLINED cover-upgrade request standing beside
   the approved correction; a careless reader treats it as the authority and, seeing
   requested_trip_cost_usd 0.00 on it, reaches the fall-through ceiling. The rule excludes it by
   speaking only of a correction the desk has approved.
 No rule reads a stamp: there is no field anywhere that names the corrected figure; the correction is
   established from the package's ledger and the approved request.
FACTOR CARD — care_ext_reration_difference (6 factors; scored adjustment_amount_usd = 127.59)
 * correction_effective_anchor (method, cross_difficulty bundle). Ladder: a package line posted after
   issue and before the journey began -> the day that line posted; a package line posted after issue
   and on or after the journey began -> the day the certificate was issued; otherwise -> the first
   day of the journey insured. Tier taken: the first. Evidence: the last routine package line posted
   2026-06-21 (5d18657a-2081-4f17-a38f-d2cdf39a2080 and e380da3b-ed49-43f4-8229-7c49a03e7ec5) against the certificate's issued_date of 2026-03-12 and
   trip_start_date of 2026-08-20, giving 75 days of cover remaining. Baseline reading: the first day
   of the journey, 15 days remaining; result then 25.52.
 * cover_term_basis (method). Ladder: a journey longer than the plan's longest single journey -> that
   maximum; a journey of that length or less on a certificate standing expired or cancelled ->
   counted from issue to the last day of the journey; otherwise -> the journey's own length. Tier
   taken: the second (15 days against TripGuard Premier's 90, and the certificate stands expired),
   giving 176 days bought. Baseline reading: the journey's own 15 days; result then 1497.11.
 * attaching_loading_basis (method). Ladder: both an age loading and a destination loading -> the
   proportion those lines bear to the base premium; one and not the other -> the plan's destination
   loading percentage; otherwise -> nothing. Tier taken: the first. Evidence rows: 7b5223ce-7572-4be8-a4e6-24c95e50a3fb (456.45)
   and 46ce914f-376b-469b-90ca-908df87a84a0 (273.87) against 587508bb-cdef-4dae-9a10-193f7ca3bb27 (1521.50), giving 1.48. Baseline reading: nothing attaches;
   result then -225.00.
 * correction_evidence_share (parameter, cross_difficulty bundle). Ladder: an approved correction
   naming its evidence and a package whose balance was settled -> the whole of it; naming its
   evidence with no balance-settling line -> eighty-five per cent; otherwise -> sixty per cent. Tier
   taken: the first. Evidence rows: care_policy_requests.d61c4a10-e061-499c-a404-ad96f7ae4641.evidence_reference = TOUR-INV-8841
   and bundle_ledger_entries.5d18657a-2081-4f17-a38f-d2cdf39a2080. Baseline reading: sixty per cent; result then 76.56.
 * charged_premium_basis (method). Ladder: a base premium with no premium returned -> the rating
   lines other than the policy fee; a base premium with premium returned -> those lines net of the
   returns; otherwise -> the figure the certificate records as premium paid. Tier taken: the first,
   giving 2251.82. Evidence rows: the four premium lines, of which 08c6e641-3280-4eb6-b31e-2139b96c54f8 is the 15.00 fee left out.
   Baseline reading: the premium paid of 2266.82, fee included; result then 121.20.
 * insured_party_uplift (parameter). Ladder: three or more insured travellers with an age loading on
   the lines -> one hundred and ten per cent; two with an age loading -> one hundred and five per
   cent; otherwise -> the whole and no more. Tier taken: the first. Evidence:
   care_policies.e2326376-824b-443f-8e1b-46046f2a9a05.insured_count = 3 and the age loading line 7b5223ce-7572-4be8-a4e6-24c95e50a3fb. Baseline reading: no
   uplift; result then 28.76.
 Whole-baseline fall-back: -419.83, a premium returned rather than charged, which is the confident
   wrong answer of an agent who found only the computation document.
 Near-miss planted: the policy fee line 08c6e641-3280-4eb6-b31e-2139b96c54f8 sits among the premium lines and a careless reader
   sweeps it into the premium already charged; the rule excludes it by naming the rating lines other
   than the policy fee, and base's own clause that the fee is never returned stands behind that.
FACTOR CARD — care_ext_cancellation_claim_intake (4 factors; scored claimed_amount_usd = 5144.85)
 * recovered_value_scope (method, cross_difficulty bundle). Ladder: a cancelled package with a credit
   standing open -> the amounts returned together with the credit at the share a credit is valued at;
   a cancelled package with no credit open -> the amounts returned; otherwise -> nothing is taken
   off. Tier taken: the first. Evidence rows: bundle_packages.dbff8373-1232-4db1-a57c-d0b30a507e6a.status = cancelled and
   credit_balance_usd = 11240.00, with the payout 041a3310-6974-4ba7-a886-d93fcc7fd7d3 at -1480.00, giving 12720.00. Baseline
   reading: nothing taken off; result then 16592.85.
 * open_credit_valuation (parameter, cross_difficulty bundle). Ladder: a transferable credit still
   redeemable after the last day of the journey -> the whole of it; a non-transferable credit still
   redeemable then -> eighty per cent; otherwise -> nothing. Tier taken: the first. Evidence: the
   Escorted Tour Package's credit_transferable is true and d7a1c870-e2a1-4187-8b09-c40ae60d68bf.credit_expires_on is 2028-02-14
   against a trip_end_date of 2026-09-03. Baseline reading: a credit is worth nothing; result then
   15260.85.
 * cancellation_promptness_share (parameter, cross_difficulty bundle). Ladder: the value-returning
   line on the ledger and the journey given up more than a fortnight before it was to begin -> the
   whole of the amount; the same line and a fortnight or less -> ninety per cent; otherwise ->
   seventy-five per cent. Tier taken: the second. Evidence: d7a1c870-e2a1-4187-8b09-c40ae60d68bf posted 2026-08-14 against a
   trip_start_date of 2026-08-20, six days. Baseline reading: seventy-five per cent; result then
   4287.38.
 * returned_deposit_share (parameter, cross_difficulty bundle). Ladder: a product that returns the
   deposit on cancellation with the package cancelled -> the whole of it; a product that does not
   with the package cancelled -> nothing; otherwise -> half of it. Tier taken: the second, because
   the Escorted Tour Package's deposit_refundable is false. Evidence: the deposit line 9490078c-d2b1-4418-8c4b-67862921de58 at
   3580.00. Baseline reading: half the deposit taken off; result then 3533.85.
 Whole-baseline fall-back: 12484.88.
 Near-miss planted: the deposit line 9490078c-d2b1-4418-8c4b-67862921de58 is prepaid and non-refundable on this product, so a
   reader who takes the ordinary half off loses 1790.00; the rule excludes it by reading the
   product's own deposit terms.
 Task-level floors: multi-source — every non-fall-through tier of outlay_evidence_basis,
 returned_value_recognition, insured_party_share, declared_ceiling_basis,
 correction_effective_anchor, correction_evidence_share, charged_premium_basis,
 insured_party_uplift, recovered_value_scope, open_credit_valuation,
 cancellation_promptness_share and returned_deposit_share combines two conditions over distinct
 evidence. Cross-difficulty: nine of the twelve read the linked vacation package or its ledger, a
 different difficulty's product, and every row they read is seeded for this traveller.

STEP 2 — TOOLS

user_scenario:
You are Rosalind Achterberg-Pike, sixty-one, a school librarian from Chicago who has been saving for a guided tour of Turkey for two years. You booked it for yourself, your husband and your daughter, and you took out travel insurance with it at the same time. In the middle of August, six days before you were due to fly, your husband's father was taken into hospital and you gave the whole trip up. The tour operator kept some of the money and gave the rest back as a voucher. You are ringing now because you want to claim on the travel insurance for what you have actually lost. You are warm and slightly apologetic on the telephone, you apologise for not ringing sooner, and you follow instructions carefully when they are explained to you.

You open with your name and the mobile number on the booking, 7732690435, and you say you are calling to put in a claim on your travel insurance because you had to cancel a holiday. If the agent asks for something more to confirm who you are, you give the last four of your passport, 1418, and if they want more still, your date of birth, 19 February 1965, and the postal code on the card, 60647. You do not offer any of those unless asked.

You have the papers in front of you. When the agent asks, you say the insurance certificate number is WLC5602841 and the tour reference is WLP7741229. You rang the emergency line the day you cancelled and they gave you a claim reference, which you read out as TC-9048-26. The operator sent you a cancellation invoice and you read its reference out as TOUR-CXL-3390. You say you cancelled on the fourteenth of August and that you were at home in Chicago when you did it, not abroad. You say the claim is in your own name, as the policyholder and the first person named on the certificate. You do not know what the voucher is worth to a claim, you do not know what the insurance will pay, and if the agent asks what you are claiming for you say the money you handed over and cannot get back, but that you would not like to put a figure on it yourself.

You have never looked at how the premium on the certificate was worked out and you would not know one line of it from another. If the agent tells you that the figure the certificate declares has to be put right before anything else, you say that makes sense, the tour cost more in the end than when you first booked it, and you leave them to it. If the agent then tells you there is a premium difference to go on the certificate because of that, you say fine, put it where it belongs, and you do not ask what it comes to unless they tell you. You agree without fuss to the desk doing anything on the certificate that is its own to do.

When the agent explains that filing the claim has to come from you and hands it over, you do it, and you can repeat back whatever it tells you if you are asked. Once the agent tells you the claim has been filed with the insurer you thank them, say you are glad it is in, and end the call. You do not ask for a copy, you do not ask for anything to be sent to you, and you do not ask how long it will take. If the agent never mentions the declared figure or the premium difference you say nothing about either, because you would have no reason to know they mattered.
